clue.text: Cleaner has iron to squash beetle

indicators.note: the cleaner squeezes around the metal, so one piece is pressed inside the other

parts.note: a char or charwoman is a British word for a cleaning lady
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A cleaner takes up an iron to flatten a bug on the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A chafer is a large beetle, such as the cockchafer or rose chafer.

clue.text: Adam's boy keeps turning up with companion, the monkey

indicators.note: holding something means the son's name goes around the other pieces

parts.note: Cain was a son of Adam in Genesis

indicators.note: turning the little word up round means it is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Adam's son keeps showing up with a friend, the ape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' signals the reversal of the small word up; CH for Companion of Honour is a British honour solvers meet often.
explanation.definitionFit: The capuchin is a small South American monkey named after the friars' hoods.

clue.text: Imposing building with a lot of produce lying on loose soil

parts.note: a crop is a quantity of produce harvested

indicators.note: loose soil is disturbed, so the four letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A large structure with a heap of harvest lying on crumbly earth.
explanation.definitionFit: An acropolis is a citadel of an ancient Greek city, often with grand temples.

clue.text: Store put on 13 with internal upheaval

parts.note: en- is a prefix meaning to put on or into, as in enthrone

indicators.note: an upheaval inside the word means its letters are thrown about and rearranged

parts.note: refers to the answer to 13 across, a word for an island

explanation.surface: A shop is placed on an island amid domestic turmoil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with internal upheaval' rearranges ISLE to SILE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensile is to store fodder in a silo to preserve it.

clue.text: A poor actor spun round and maanged to meet one princess

indicators.note: turning round means the pair of pieces before it is read backwards

parts.note: a ham is an actor who overacts badly
the printed misspelling of 'managed'; managed means ran, as in ran a business
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A bad actor twirls about and contrives to be introduced to a royal lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spun round' turns A HAM into MAHA. The clue as published misspells 'managed' as 'maanged'; the sense is unaffected.
explanation.definitionFit: A maharani is an Indian princess or the wife of a maharajah.

clue.text: A right badly hurt Labour unlikely to embrace fine Conservative PM

indicators.note: badly hurt suggests the word is knocked out of shape, so its letters are rearranged
hugging the letter for fine puts it inside the rearranged party name
an unlikely form of the party name is a scrambled one

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A right-winger badly wounds a Labour party that will hardly welcome a fine Tory premier.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagram signals: 'badly' works on hurt and 'unlikely' on Labour, while 'to embrace' places the fine letter inside the second. Balfour led a Conservative government.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Balfour was Conservative Prime Minister of Britain from 1902 to 1905.

clue.text: Expose fellow that's spoken communication — to go quickly

parts.note: to air is to expose, as views or laundry

indicators.note: a word that is spoken is heard rather than seen, so a sound-alike is wanted

parts.note: a fellow is a male

explanation.surface: Reveal the man who sent an urgent message to be delivered fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmail is post carried by aircraft so that it arrives quickly.

clue.text: What may be brought by gangster with gun?

definitions.text: What may be brought by gangster with gun?

parts.note: Al Capone was the notorious Chicago gangster
an arm is a weapon such as a gun

explanation.surface: An armed mobster causes panic.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunman's arrival raises an alarm, a warning cry of danger.

clue.text: Home team locked up

parts.note: in means at home
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: The home side is confined.
explanation.definitionFit: Inside is slang for in prison, as in doing time.

clue.text: City rector's area, not the East End

indicators.note: Cockneys of London's East End famously drop their aitches, so the H is left off

parts.note: a rector serves a parish

explanation.surface: A clergyman's district is described as not being in a deprived part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: London's East End is the home of Cockney speech, which drops the H sound; here it also points at the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris is the capital city of France.

clue.text: Mum is collecting almost all the textiles

parts.note: mater is Latin, and old British slang, for mother

indicators.note: gathering something up means the word is wraps round another piece

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: nearly all of the word means its final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Mother is gathering up nearly all the fabric in the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Materials are cloths or fabrics, the same as textiles.

clue.text: MIT man, I teach a struggling student engaged with combinatorics?

indicators.note: struggling words are twisted about, so all these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An academic at MIT says he teaches a struggling pupil about counting arrangements.
explanation.definitionFit: Combinatorics is a branch of mathematics, so someone working in it is one of these.

clue.text: Whimper detected in pet maybe — one in an Italian family

indicators.note: a sound detected in an animal is found inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a cat is an example of a pet, hence 'maybe'
to pule is to whine or whimper

explanation.surface: A whining noise is heard from a household animal, the creature belonging to an Italian household.
explanation.walkthrough: The Capulets are Juliet's family in Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet, set in Verona.
explanation.definitionFit: A Capulet belongs to the Veronese family feuding with the Montagues in Shakespeare.

clue.text: Not able to go into battle, having lost certain members

definitions.text: Not able to go into battle
definitions.meaning: without weapons, so not equipped to fight

explanation.definitionFit: Unarmed means weaponless, and humorously also lacking arms as body parts.

clue.text: Passage with entrance sealed off in cut-off location

indicators.note: closing the entrance means the word's first letter is removed

parts.note: an aisle is a passage between rows of seats

explanation.surface: A corridor whose door has been blocked becomes a remote spot.
explanation.definitionFit: An isle is an island, a place cut off from the mainland by water.

clue.text: Fresh things for Wimbledon dance featured in TV bulletin?

indicators.note: an item featured in a programme appears within it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a news bulletin on television
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A tennis tournament event gets a mention in a television news broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the London tennis championship, where umpires call for new balls at set intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis balls are replaced with new ones regularly during matches at Wimbledon.

clue.text: Rugby players in another fracas

parts.note: a second one is another
a row is a noisy quarrel

explanation.surface: Rugby players caught up in a fresh brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: The second row is the pair of locks in a rugby scrum.

clue.text: Journalist about to meet man on station platform?

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a porter carries luggage at a railway station

explanation.surface: A newspaper writer is about to meet someone on a train platform.
explanation.definitionFit: A reporter is a journalist who gathers and writes news.

clue.text: Thus starts to cuddle intimate friend at a party?

definitions.text: Thus starts to cuddle intimate friend at a party?

parts.note: so means thus, in this way

indicators.note: the starts of the two following words means their first letters

parts.note: an ally is a friend, as in a political party

explanation.surface: Someone at a party begins to cuddle a close friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaving socially means mixing with others, as at a party with friends.

clue.text: Bravo! I'll come just after, man!

definitions.text: Bravo! I'll come just after, man!

parts.words: Bravo! I'll come just after, man!
parts.note: in the radio alphabet the code word for C follows Bravo, and it is also a man's name

explanation.surface: Someone cheers and promises to follow straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bravo!' looks like applause, but it is the code word for B in the NATO phonetic alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie is the NATO code word for C, the letter after B, and a man's name.

clue.text: Some land in which a gang is cut short

indicators.note: cutting short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a crew is a gang of workers or criminals

explanation.surface: A plot of ground where a gang has been curtailed.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of land area, about 4,047 square metres.

clue.text: Most competent adult in supremely happy state

parts.note: A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult
blest, an old form of blessed, means in bliss

explanation.surface: A grown-up in a state of perfect happiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Ablest is the superlative of able, meaning the most capable.

clue.text: Girl holding ball for the whole world

indicators.note: clasping something means the girl's word surrounds the other piece

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
a lob is a high ball in tennis or cricket

explanation.surface: A girl clutches a ball meant for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Global means worldwide, covering the entire world.

clue.text: Holiday island embracing English language

indicators.note: hugging another piece means the island's name goes around it

parts.note: Bali is an Indonesian resort island

explanation.surface: A tourist island welcomes English speakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Bengali is the language of Bangladesh and West Bengal.

clue.text: Refusal to eat a Chinese if it's Mexican food you want

indicators.note: eating something takes it inside, so the refusal goes around the other pieces

parts.note: no is a refusal

explanation.surface: Declining a Chinese takeaway because you want Mexican.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacho is a tortilla chip, a Mexican snack usually topped with cheese.

clue.text: A bit of Florida — golden territory that needs nothing more

parts.note: or is the heraldic term for gold
land is territory
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Part of the Sunshine State is golden ground that lacks nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Orlando is a city in central Florida, home to Disney World.

clue.text: Lover no longer recoils terribly when there's an old poem

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: doing something terribly means doing it in a muddle, so the letters of recoils are rearranged

explanation.surface: A former partner shrinks back in horror at an antique piece of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Excelsior is an 1841 poem by Longfellow about a youth climbing an Alpine pass.

clue.text: Female wearing this hat would be widow-like

indicators.note: the female letter goes inside the answer, which wears it, so it is the longer word minus that letter
says the longer word is what would result, so taking the letter out gives the answer

parts.note: bereft means bereaved, as a widow is

explanation.surface: A woman wearing a certain headgear would look like a widow.
explanation.walkthrough: An unusual clue with the definition in the middle: put F inside the answer and you get BEREFT, so the answer is BEREFT without its F.
explanation.definitionFit: A beret is a round flat soft cap.

clue.text: Worthless pony went berserk

indicators.note: going wild means the letters of pony went are jumbled

explanation.surface: A small horse ran amok.
explanation.definitionFit: Twopenny describes something cheap and trifling, worth only two old pennies.

clue.text: Minimal grass gets cow to look angry

indicators.note: the least part of the word, its first letter, is taken

parts.note: to lower (rhyming with power) is to frown or scowl, and a cow lows

explanation.surface: A scrap of grass makes a cow scowl.
explanation.walkthrough: LOWER here is read as 'one that lows', a cow; it is also a word for scowling, rhyming with power.
explanation.definitionFit: To glower is to stare angrily or sullenly.
